title: Homework for table-level choices: planted truths with traps, the product's own rules, states built as production builds them
request: Phase 7 (the owner): a student behind every choice; 29.2 first in the suggested order: homework with known answers for the technical choices 22.1 did not reach.
plan: Plant the truth of four table-level choices in invented tables, with traps where the rules fail.
Call the product's own rules on each table.
Build each decision's state the way production builds it.
Write per-point sets with a sealed partition by table, through the same builder as every set.

decisions.decision: Four points by construction; the column choices go to the language model (29.9) and six choices to measured outcomes (29.3).
decisions.why: A classifier on one state cannot rank a table's columns; a metric, a recipe or a threshold is right by what was measured after it, not by a plant.

decisions.decision: One state builder (ledger/states.py) for production capture and the homework.
decisions.why: A student trained on fields production never records would answer every real decision from its intercept.

decisions.decision: Names from pools shared across truths, and every table also with its names hidden, one group.
decisions.why: Names drawn per truth let a student read the answer from the name.

decisions.decision: The split rule is default_split on propose()'s first time and group candidates.
decisions.why: That is what the product declares (the wizard); the data card's purposes are not what runs.

change: dclab_core/benchgen2.py; dclab_rnd/decisions_gen.py (decide_v2, build_v2, --v2); dclab_rnd/ledger/states.py and its use in capture (task, split, cases, every column's cleaning step with the raw bands) and the pipeline; ledger STATE_FIELDS; the lake, the register, the trainer and the archive read generated_v2; dclab-core 0.66.0; tests.

findings.defect: The planted truth could be read from the state's names.
findings.scenario: Grouping by name tokens alone scored 100% on task.framing and data.cleaning_step; country and app_version were always none; the cases flags gave one pattern per variant (the fitted card 1.0 on dev).
findings.cause: Names and flags were drawn per truth.
findings.fix: Shared name pools, hidden-name twins in one group, the cases signals varied within each variant; a name-only guess is now at chance.

findings.defect: The split rule recorded was not the product's.
findings.scenario: The v2 rule read the data card's purposes; Home declares the proposal's first time candidate and no group, the wizard the first time and group candidates; they differed on 80 of 160 seeds.
findings.cause: The rule was rebuilt rather than called as the product calls it.
findings.fix: default_split on propose()'s candidates (the wizard's declaration); the rule is now right on 48%, not the 75% of a rule that never runs.

findings.defect: Some planted truths a careful data scientist would dispute.
findings.scenario: A transaction table with a fraud reason on every row read as cases; a contract start or first-seen date can be the right split key.
findings.cause: Variants drawn too close to the other side's.
findings.fix: Payment notes, mostly empty and never a fraud's kind; only dates that are never a row's time, one per entity.

findings.defect: A rare binary table could have no positive.
findings.scenario: Three tables with a constant target labelled binary, one in the sealed partition.
findings.cause: The positives were drawn at 1 to 5% of 300 rows.

findings.defect: The homework's states did not match what production records.
findings.scenario: Production recorded rows and columns for the task and cases, has_time and has_groups for the split, only applied steps for cleaning.
findings.fix: One builder (ledger/states.py) for both; production now records the same fields, every column's cleaning step or none.

findings.defect: Ten of the fourteen points were not built, against the plan's Part A.
findings.scenario: Part A listed six choices as true by construction.
findings.cause: Part A was written before the points were studied.
findings.fix: Part A corrected: two column choices to 29.9, six to measured outcomes in 29.3, two not decided today.

findings.defect: The new tests skipped instead of failing when a new module broke.
findings.scenario: A failed import of benchgen2 skipped the whole file.
findings.cause: The new modules' imports sat inside the ImportError guard.
findings.fix: Only numpy and pandas are guarded.

measurements.name: the v2 homework
measurements.gate: each built point: 2,000 decisions or more over 100 groups or more, both labels, a sealed partition, reproducible
measurements.result: 1,200 table pairs, 21,600 decisions: task.framing 2,400 (rule right 80%), split.strategy 2,400 (48%), data.cases_table 2,400 (54%), data.cleaning_step 14,400 (73%); a name-only guess at chance
measurements.against_gate: Met for the four built points; the manifest records the rules' accuracy.
limits: Invented tables: the scores say how a model reads these traps, not real tables.
Home's build declares no group: its split rule is weaker than the wizard's measured here.

measurements.name: the four students on their dev rows
measurements.gate: none fixed: each student beside its rule on dev, with intervals; the sealed partition unread
measurements.result: task.framing 0.916 [0.888, 0.937] against the rule's 0.790; split.strategy 0.772 [0.734, 0.806] against 0.504; data.cases_table 0.883 [0.853, 0.908] against 0.541; data.cleaning_step 0.922 [0.912, 0.932] against 0.726
measurements.against_gate: Not scored: dev rows of invented tables; promotion needs the sealed gate and real decisions.
limits: Dev holds new seeds of the same generators, not new kinds of table.

outcome: Four more choices have homework with known answers, read the way production records them.
lessons: A planted truth must not be readable from anything but what it is about: draw names from shared pools and hide them in twins.
Call the product's rule where the product calls it; a reimplementation measures a rule that never runs.
risks: The students of these points are not in shadow until production has recorded decisions with the new states.
